drivers.name: Promotion: 20% off
drivers.evidence: Past 20% off: noise-adjusted x2.09; this week's price is deeper (16.4% off), but not as deep as 30% off events (x3.32). Seasonal context supports uplift, but baseline already captures some of it.

drivers.name: Week after promotion (pantry loading)
drivers.evidence: Past week after promotion: median x0.82 (noise-adjusted x0.8). This week is not immediately after a promotion, but the prior promotion (2026-08-24) was 3 weeks ago—no direct overlap.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: No prior delivery issues; warning is vague. Low confidence. No evidence of actual disruption.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is similar to past 20% off events (x1.99, x2.09 noise-adjusted), but the current price is deeper (16.4% off vs 20% off) and the product is in a high-traffic season (back-to-school). The baseline already reflects recent seasonal lift. The supplier warning adds downside risk, but no delivery delay has occurred. The classical model's x2.09 is over-optimistic—this week's promotion is not as deep as past 30% off events, and the prior week's promotion (x0.82) suggests some demand shift. Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited data and overlapping drivers.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Promotion: 20% off
  shelf price: 8.26 (-16.4% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.9 - 233.3 | 10%-90%: 67.4 - 191.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
